findings.message: contains multiple layers of encoding (hex/base64/unicode escapes) (5 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Avoid multi-layer encoding; it hindles review and may indicate malicious intent.
findings.impact: Multi-layer encoding (hex/base64/unicode) significantly hinders security review.
findings.attack_vector: Chained decoding layers — attacker increases analysis cost and may hide malicious payloads.

findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads a likely secret source and opens a network connection in the same source file
findings.remediation: Keep secrets out of agent-visible output and require an allowlisted destination before egress.
findings.impact: A nearby secret source and network sink create a plausible credential-exposure path requiring data-flow review.
findings.attack_vector: Production code reads a non-environment secret source and opens a network connection within a bounded call-site window.

findings.remediation: Remove embedded credentials, rotate exposed secrets, and load them only from a protected secret store.

findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and use a fixed allowlisted command with bounded arguments.

findings.message: uses Error.stack or stack trace inspection for anti-debugging
findings.remediation: Avoid stack-based anti-debugging techniques; they indicate malicious intent.
findings.impact: Stack inspection can support anti-analysis behavior, but is also common in diagnostics and error reporting.
findings.attack_vector: Source reads Error.stack or invokes a trace helper; reviewer must determine intent.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: constructs a regular expression from a non-literal value (possible ReDoS) (4 occurrences in this file)
findings.basis: OWASP Regular Expression Denial of Service Prevention
findings.remediation: Use bounded, allowlisted patterns and enforce input and execution limits for dynamic regular expressions.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled regular expression can consume excessive CPU and deny service.
findings.attack_vector: A non-literal value is passed to RegExp without pattern or execution bounds.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses string concatenation or char-code construction to hide keywords (5 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use readable, explicit code patterns; avoid character-code obfuscation.
findings.impact: Character-code construction hides string literals from grep-based detection.
findings.attack_vector: String.fromCharCode() builds dangerous strings at runtime — evades static patterns.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
